name: Habitat Challenge 2020 PointNav
ability_definition: The ability to know your location in relation to the environment or to know where other objects are in relation to you.

task_realism.reasoning: The agent moves through photorealistic 3D scans of real, previously unseen buildings. It must keep track of its own position without GPS or compass while moving toward a goal. This closely resembles the core of workplace indoor wayfinding, such as a technician, firefighter, or delivery worker in an unfamiliar building. However, real work rarely supplies the goal as exact relative coordinates. Workers usually rely on landmarks, signage, maps, or verbal directions. The environments are also limited to residential and office interiors.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Several conditions are realistic. Sensor noise and actuation noise are modeled on a real LoCoBot, there is no odometry, and the environments are novel. These are real strengths over noiseless settings. Other conditions are not realistic. The scenes are static, with no people, moving obstacles, lighting changes, or doors. There is no time pressure and no consequence for errors beyond the score. The simulation also leaves a sim-to-real gap. Performance is averaged over many short episodes rather than sustained operation.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark captures two parts of the ability: knowing one's own location through path integration, and knowing where a single goal lies relative to oneself. It does not test awareness of multiple surrounding objects or people. It also omits orientation to cardinal directions or maps, large outdoor or vehicle-scale navigation, three-dimensional orientation such as aviation, and re-orientation after getting lost. The result is a meaningful but narrow slice of the ability: egocentric dead-reckoning toward a point.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs are egocentric RGB-D camera views, which resemble what a real embodied worker perceives. The outputs are discrete low-level actions: move 0.25 m, turn 30°, or stop. The goal is specified as numeric displacement coordinates. Neither the action format nor the goal format matches how people receive or carry out navigation tasks at work, and success is judged by stopping within a fixed radius.

transferability_reasoning: Habitat 2020 PointNav is one of the more direct tests of embodied spatial orientation. It uses realistic noisy perception and unfamiliar real-building scans, and it requires the agent to track its own position without odometry. Transfer is limited by static simulated scenes and artificial coordinate-based goals. It is also limited because it covers only point-goal dead-reckoning, not broader awareness of surrounding objects, maps, or outdoor and vehicle orientation.

2020.model_or_system: DAN / SLAM-net with D* planning (Karkus et al.)
2020.metric: SPL (success weighted by path length), percentage points (0-100)
2020.human_reference: General adult navigating an unfamiliar indoor building from an egocentric view. They are given the goal as coordinates relative to where they started, with noisy movement and no GPS or compass.
